title: py-repair-kit: Python bug-repair tasks on a small bookkeeping library
summary: Five issue-style repair tasks on ledgerlite, a small stdlib-only Python 3.12 bookkeeping library. In each episode an agent reads files, edits library modules, runs a visible test and submits. A hidden pytest suite grades the final workspace offline and deterministically.

claims.text: The purchased product contains exactly 5 tasks (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5). A separate set of 2 seller-supplied audit tasks is disclosed. It is not delivered and is not counted in the 5.
claims.check: tasks/ contains exactly five task directories, each with a task.json; manifest taskCount = 5, auditTaskCount = 2.

claims.text: Target skills, one per task: T1 data-structure invariants (LRU recency ordering); T2 text ingestion robustness (encodings, CSV headers); T3 exact decimal arithmetic (cent allocation, rounding); T4 time-based algorithms (token-bucket rate limiting with an injected clock); T5 timezone- and boundary-correct period logic across two modules.
claims.check: targetSkill field of each tasks/<id>/task.json; the files each reference solution changes.

claims.text: Seller-assigned difficulty labels: 2 easy (T1, T2), 2 medium (T3, T4), 1 hard (T5). The hard task needs changes in two library modules.
claims.check: difficulty field of each task.json; solutions/T5/ contains two files.

claims.text: The ledgerlite library and the environment driver (grader/) use only the Python 3.12 standard library. The only third-party packages are pytest 8.3.5, pluggy 1.6.0, iniconfig 2.3.0 and packaging 26.3. They are used only to run visible and hidden tests, and requirements.lock pins them by exact version and sha256 hash.
claims.check: imports in src/ and grader/; requirements.lock.

claims.text: Runs on CPython 3.12. The runner image is built from Dockerfile.runner on python:3.12-slim pinned by digest sha256:78387bc3881b8273120a12ebe6c1ab22b018ccc2c9adf565ae1ac9b536e184ea and runs as a non-root user. No GPU or accelerator is needed.
claims.check: Dockerfile.runner FROM line and USER line.

claims.text: Fully offline. Resetting, stepping, running visible tests and grading need no network access. scripts/verify.sh --docker runs every task with --network none.

Deterministic. The environment has no randomness: the reset seed is recorded but does not change task content. Tests inject fake clocks, and graders run with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and TZ=UTC. Grading the same final workspace again gives the same score, passed and failed counts.
claims.check: grader/tasks.py child environment; scripts/verify_tasks.py grades each solved task twice and compares.

claims.text: Each episode allows 12 tool actions (list_files, read_file, write_file, run_visible_tests) plus a final submit, which does not count against the budget, and 600 seconds of wall-clock time. A visible-test run times out after 60 s and hidden grading after 120 s. An episode that ends by budget exhaustion or timeout scores 0.
claims.check: actionBudget, timeBudgetSec and gradeTimeoutSec in each task.json; grader/env.py.

claims.text: On each purchased task's starting state, at least one hidden test fails. With the reference solution applied, every hidden test passes.
Every purchased task's hidden test suite contains at least 8 test cases as collected by pytest.
claims.check: PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest --collect-only -q tasks/<id>/tests for each purchased task.

claims.text: Each task has a visible test separate from its hidden tests. Hidden tests are never copied into the agent workspace. Grading rebuilds the starting state and copies in only the files matching the task's editable patterns (ledgerlite/*.py, excluding conftest.py).

Delivery includes the full library source, all 5 purchased tasks (statement, starting-state overlay, visible tests, hidden tests), a reference solution for each purchased task in solutions/, the grader and environment driver, requirements.lock, Dockerfile.runner and the verification scripts.
Every task, including grading, runs inside a container limited to 1 CPU, 512 MB of memory and 128 processes, with a read-only root filesystem and a 256 MB tmpfs at /tmp.
claims.check: Run scripts/verify.sh --docker, which applies exactly these limits.

claims.text: src/ledgerlite has 8 modules plus __init__.py, with fewer than 1,000 lines of Python in total.
